answer.rationale: The release timing (2h ago) aligns with the start of the latency climb (90 min ago), making the new build the prime suspect. memory_b1 documents a precedent: rolling back during an error spike restored checkout cleanly without customer impact, and the prior build was stable. Given the primary region is the only affected surface, the problem is release-bound rather than capacity- or partner-bound, so circuit breakers would risk dropping writes and failover would risk in-flight settlement writes at peak — both directly conflict with the objective of preserving customer writes. A targeted rollback is the single intervention most likely to restore write p99 quickly while keeping writes intact. memory_b1 will be verified before commit to reconfirm that the prior build remained stable under similar load and that the rollback completed without customer-visible effect.
